title: Travel in Europe
description: An easy on-ramp through Europe's cities, landmarks, railways, and quirks.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of France?
questions.explanation: Paris has been the capital of France since the 12th century and is the country's largest city (Wikipedia: 'Paris').

questions.prompt: Madrid is the capital of which country?
questions.explanation: Madrid is the capital and most populous city of Spain, sitting almost exactly in the centre of the Iberian Peninsula (Wikipedia: 'Madrid').

questions.prompt: The Danube, Europe's second-longest river, flows through which of these capital cities?
questions.explanation: The Danube runs through Budapest, dividing the historic halves of Buda and Pest. Prague sits on the Vltava, Warsaw on the Vistula, and Madrid on the Manzanares (Wikipedia: 'Danube').

questions.prompt: The ancient Colosseum amphitheatre is a famous landmark in which city?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum, completed around AD 80, stands in the centre of Rome and is the largest ancient amphitheatre ever built (Wikipedia: 'Colosseum').

questions.prompt: The still-unfinished Sagrada Família basilica in Barcelona was designed by which architect?
questions.explanation: Antoni Gaudí took over the Sagrada Família in 1883 and worked on it until his death in 1926; construction continues today (Wikipedia: 'Sagrada Família').

questions.prompt: The Channel Tunnel, used by Eurostar trains, runs beneath the sea to connect which two countries?
questions.explanation: The 50 km Channel Tunnel links Folkestone in England with Coquelles in France beneath the English Channel; Eurostar has run through it since 1994 (Wikipedia: 'Channel Tunnel').

questions.prompt: "ICE" (InterCity Express) is the high-speed train brand of which country's national railway?
questions.explanation: ICE trains are operated by Deutsche Bahn in Germany; France's equivalent is the TGV and Spain's is the AVE (Wikipedia: 'Intercity-Express').

questions.prompt: Which of these countries uses the euro as its official currency?
questions.explanation: Germany adopted the euro in 1999/2002. Sweden uses the krona, Switzerland the franc, and Norway the krone — none of those three use the euro (Wikipedia: 'Eurozone').

questions.prompt: Basque (Euskara), a language with no known relation to any other in Europe, is spoken in parts of which two neighbouring countries?
questions.explanation: Basque is spoken in the Basque Country straddling the western Pyrenees in northern Spain and south-western France. It is a language isolate, unrelated to the Indo-European languages around it (Wikipedia: 'Basque language').

questions.prompt: Surströmming — fermented Baltic herring famous for its pungent smell — is a traditional delicacy of which country?
questions.explanation: Surströmming is a Swedish speciality of lightly salted herring fermented for months, so notoriously smelly that it is usually opened outdoors (Wikipedia: 'Surströmming').
